detail.vintage: AER ST3 actuals through 2026-08 (ST3 file vintage 28 September 2026; loaded 2026-10-04); seasonal baseline forecast, built 2026-10-04; nowcast (seasonal baseline + confirmed maintenance), built 2026-10-04
detail.method: Residual: ST3 mined plus ST3 in-situ minus ST3 sent for further processing (taken as a positive number), from the approved ST3 lines. The sent-for-further-processing line (bitumen fed to upgraders) is kept in the data but is not a visible row: it is an intermediate manufacturing transfer, not a market stream. Never a plug: it is the remainder, not a number chosen to balance.
detail.why: Raw bitumen that does not feed an upgrader: the pool that can be blended into dilbit (ST3 mined plus in-situ bitumen, less bitumen sent for further processing). It becomes dilbit only after blending with diluent (roughly 25-35% diluent by volume). The blend pool is steam-assisted gravity drainage (SAGD) bitumen minus the share bound for upgraders, plus mined bitumen from Kearl and Fort Hills; mined bitumen at Horizon, Syncrude, and Suncor Base is locked to their upgraders by plant configuration and is never blended. Bitumen sent for further processing (the upgrader feed) is a manufacturing transfer, not a market stream, so it is not shown as a row; the bitumen number already excludes it. This is the grade whose availability gets tight during Suncor/Syncrude turnarounds, because redirected flows and flexible barrels from SAGD and PFT (paraffinic froth treatment) mines land in dilbit differently every event. Coker 8-2 accounting: the Syncrude mine dial-back (Aug -35.4, Sep -91.4, Oct -26.6 kb/d bitumen) is shown for context only and does not reduce tradable heavy; the event's market impact is on synthetic crude only (Sep 2026 -77.0 kb/d gross coker rate, no redirect between plants). Cleanest precedent: Q1 2026, when Suncor non-upgraded bitumen rose to 279.5 kb/d 'primarily due to decreased upgrader availability.'
detail.extra: Project mapping (conceptual): the dilbit blend pool is steam-assisted gravity drainage (SAGD) bitumen minus the upgrader-bound share plus Kearl and Fort Hills mined bitumen; mined bitumen at Horizon, Syncrude, and Suncor Base is upgrader-locked and never blended. The ST3 lines do not support a project-level dilbit split, so the grade is the residual; no split is shown and nothing is invented. Disposition defaults: PFT (paraffinic froth treatment) mines send their barrels to the most profitable outlet; SAGD output is unchanged by upgrader outages, with the upgrader-bound share assumed diverted to dilbit.
detail.nowcast: Mined + in-situ - sent for further processing on nowcast inputs; the Coker mine dial-back sits on the Syncrude mined-bitumen row.

detail.why: MEMO row: the outages already reflected in the project and plant rows (Horizon, Syncrude Coker 8-2, Suncor Base Plant, Cold Lake, Christina Lake F/G). It lists the outages for reference and is NOT subtracted again in the storage balance. Oct 2026 (164.4): Horizon -119, Syncrude Coker 8-2 tail -22.4, Cenovus Christina Lake F/G tail -20 (assumed carryover, not company-stated), Cold Lake -3. Nov 2026 (23.0): Suncor Base Plant -15 bitumen and -5 SCO (quarterly rate; timing within Q4 unpublished, placed mid-quarter), Cold Lake -3. Dec 2026 (3.0): Cold Lake -3. Jan 2027 onward: no company-confirmed maintenance in the forecast. Two cadence-modeled events are in the numbers, labeled as such everywhere, never as company-confirmed: Primrose/Wolf Lake Apr 2027 (-26 kb/d; the April-dip pattern has weakened in recent years) and MacKay River Sep 2027 (-12 kb/d). No other 2027 turnarounds are modeled. Per-event detail lives on the Maintenance tab.
detail.nowcast: Aug 2026 nowcast 32.8 kb/d offline: Syncrude Coker 8-2 Aug 20-31 (77 kb/d for 12 of 31 days = 29.8) plus Cold Lake Q3 turnaround -3 (Imperial guidance). Sep 2026 nowcast 310.0 kb/d offline: Horizon -230 (September share of the Sep 8 35-day turnaround, per ruling 2026-09-22), Coker 8-2 full month -77.0, Cold Lake -3. No other confirmed events fall in the gap; Suncor Base Plant Q4 cuts sit in Oct-Dec only. MEMO: these outages are already reflected in the project and plant rows, and this line is not subtracted again in the storage balance.

detail.why: The AER reporting adjustment: the disposition-side plug the AER uses to force total supply to equal total disposition. Actuals show the reported value; forecast months carry its trailing-12-month mean (+95.5 kb/d, recomputed each build). Persistently positive (mean +56 kb/d over 199 months), so it is subtracted in the balance. Carried as its own disclosed line, never buried in supply, and never entering the five marketed supply rows.

detail.why: The exact AER ST3 inventory balance: supply total (maintenance is already reflected in the supply rows, so there is no separate maintenance term; the Maintenance offline row is a memo) plus total receipts minus losses (flare, fuel, shrinkage) plus ST3 adjustments minus Alberta use minus removals minus the AER reporting adjustment (the plug row below). Matches the reported change in closing inventory in all 200 history months within 0.1 kb/d. Negative means oil drawn out of commercial storage.
detail.nowcast: Physical supply balance on nowcast inputs: supply total plus diluent imports minus Alberta use minus removals. Maintenance outages are already reflected in the nowcast project and plant rows; the maint line is a memo, not subtracted. Negative means oil drawn out of commercial storage.
